            <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 11pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">TRANSOCEAN
LTD. AND SUBSIDIARIES</font></div>
            <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 11pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow"><a name="Notes">NOTES</a> TO CONDENSED CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></div>
            <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">(Unaudited)</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 11pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">Note&#160;1&#8212;Nature
of Business</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">Transocean&#160;Ltd.
(together with its subsidiaries and predecessors, unless the context requires
otherwise, &#8220;Transocean,&#8221; the &#8220;Company,&#8221; &#8220;we,&#8221; &#8220;us&#8221; or &#8220;our&#8221;) is a leading
international provider of offshore contract drilling services for oil and gas
wells.&#160;&#160;Our mobile offshore drilling fleet is considered one of the
most modern and versatile fleets in the world.&#160;&#160;Specializing in
technically demanding sectors of the offshore drilling business with a
particular focus on deepwater and harsh environment drilling services, we
contract our drilling rigs, related equipment and work crews predominantly on a
dayrate basis to drill oil and gas wells.&#160;&#160;At March&#160;31, 2010, we
owned, had partial ownership interests in or operated 140<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">&#160;</font>mobile offshore
drilling units.&#160;&#160;As of this date, our fleet consisted of 46<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">&#160;</font>High-Specification
Floaters (Ultra-Deepwater, Deepwater and Harsh Environment semisubmersibles and
drillships), 26<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">&#160;</font>Midwater
Floaters, 10&#160;High-Specification Jackups, 55&#160;Standard Jackups and
three<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">&#160;</font>Other
Rigs (see Note&#160;15&#8212;Subsequent Events).&#160;&#160;We also have&#160;three
Ultra-Deepwater Floaters under construction (see Note&#160;8&#8212;Drilling Fleet
Expansion and Dispositions).</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">We also
provide oil and gas drilling management services, drilling engineering and
drilling project management services, and we participate in oil and gas
exploration and production activities.&#160;&#160;Drilling management services
are provided through Applied Drilling Technology Inc., our wholly owned
subsidiary, and through ADT International, a division of one of our U.K.
subsidiaries (together, &#8220;ADTI&#8221;).&#160;&#160;ADTI conducts drilling management
services primarily on either a dayrate or a completed-project, fixed-price (or
&#8220;turnkey&#8221;) basis.&#160;&#160;Oil and gas properties consist of exploration,
development and production activities performed by Challenger Minerals Inc. and
Challenger Minerals (North Sea) Limited (together, &#8220;CMI&#8221;), our oil and gas
subsidiaries.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 11pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">Note&#160;2&#8212;Significant
Accounting Policies</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Basis of presentation</font>&#8212;Our
accompanying condensed consolidated financial statements have been prepared
without audit in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the
United States (&#8220;U.S.&#8221;) for interim financial information and with the
instructions to Form&#160;10-Q and Article&#160;10 of Regulation&#160;S-X of the
U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (&#8220;SEC&#8221;).&#160;&#160;Pursuant to such
rules and regulations, these financial statements do not include all disclosures
required by accounting principles generally accepted in the U.S. for complete
financial statements.&#160;&#160;The condensed consolidated financial statements
reflect all adjustments, which are, in the opinion of management, necessary for
a fair presentation of financial position, results of operations and cash flows
for the interim periods.&#160;&#160;Such adjustments are considered to be of a
normal recurring nature unless otherwise identified.&#160;&#160;Operating
results for the three months ended March&#160;31, 2010 are not necessarily
indicative of the results that may be expected for the year ending
December&#160;31, 2010 or for any future period.&#160;&#160;The accompanying
condensed consolidated financial statements and notes thereto should be read in
conjunction with the audited consolidated financial statements and notes thereto
included in our&#160;annual report&#160;on Form&#160;10-K for the year ended
December&#160;31, 2009.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Accounting estimates</font>&#8212;The
preparation of financial statements in accordance with accounting principles
generally accepted in the U.S. requires us to make estimates and assumptions
that affect the reported amounts of assets, liabilities, revenues and expenses
and the disclosures of contingent assets and liabilities.&#160;&#160;On an
ongoing basis, we evaluate our estimates and assumptions, including those
related to our allowance for doubtful accounts, materials and supplies
obsolescence, property and equipment, investments, notes receivable, goodwill
and other intangible assets, income taxes, share-based compensation, defined
benefit pension plans and other postretirement benefits and
contingencies.&#160;&#160;We base our estimates and assumptions on historical
experience and on various other factors we believe are reasonable under the
circumstances, the results of which form the basis for making judgments about
the carrying amounts of assets and liabilities that are not readily apparent
from other sources.&#160;&#160;Actual results could differ from such
estimates.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Fair value measurements</font>&#8212;We
estimate fair value at a price that would be received to sell an asset or paid
to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants in
the principal market for the asset or liability.&#160;&#160;Our valuation
techniques require inputs that we categorize using a three-level hierarchy as
follows: (1)&#160;unadjusted quoted prices for identical assets or liabilities
in active markets (&#8220;Level&#160;1&#8221;), (2)&#160;direct or indirect observable
inputs, including quoted prices or other market data, for similar assets or
liabilities in active markets or identical assets or liabilities in less active
markets (&#8220;Level&#160;2&#8221;) and (3)&#160;unobservable inputs that require
significant judgment for which there is little or no market data
(&#8220;Level&#160;3&#8221;).&#160;&#160;When multiple input levels are required for a
valuation, we categorize the entire fair value measurement according to the
lowest level input that is significant to the measurement even though we may
have also utilized significant inputs that are more readily
observable.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Principles of consolidation</font>&#8212;We
consolidate those investments that meet the criteria of a variable interest
entity where we are deemed to be the primary beneficiary for accounting purposes
and for entities in which we have a majority voting
interest.&#160;&#160;Intercompany transactions and accounts are eliminated in
consolidation.&#160;&#160;For investments in joint ventures and other entities
that do not meet the criteria of a variable interest entity or where we are not
deemed to be the primary beneficiary for accounting purposes of those entities
that meet the variable interest entity criteria, we use the equity method of
accounting if we have the ability to exercise significant influence over the
unconsolidated affiliate.&#160;&#160;We use the cost method of accounting for
investments in joint ventures and other entities if we do not have the ability
to exercise significant influence over the unconsolidated
affiliate.&#160;&#160;See Note&#160;4&#8212;Variable Interest Entities.</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 11pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">Note&#160;3&#8212;New
Accounting Pronouncements</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">Recently
Adopted Accounting Standards</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Consolidation</font>&#8212;Effective
January&#160;1, 2010, we adopted the accounting standards update that requires
enhanced transparency of our involvement with variable interest entities, which
(a)&#160;amends certain guidance for determining whether an enterprise is a
variable interest entity, (b)&#160;requires a qualitative rather than a
quantitative analysis to determine the primary beneficiary, and
(c)&#160;requires continuous assessments of whether an enterprise is the primary
beneficiary of a variable interest entity.&#160;&#160;We evaluated these
requirements, particularly with regard to our interests in Transocean Pacific
Drilling Inc. (&#8220;TPDI&#8221;) and Angola Deepwater Drilling Company Limited (&#8220;ADDCL&#8221;)
and our adoption did not have a material effect on our condensed consolidated
statement of financial position, results of operations or cash
flows.&#160;&#160;See Note&#160;4&#8212;Variable Interest Entities.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Fair value measurements and
disclosures</font>&#8212;Effective January&#160;1, 2010, we adopted the effective
provisions of the accounting standards update that clarifies existing disclosure
requirements and introduces additional disclosure requirements for fair value
measurements.&#160;&#160;The update requires entities to disclose the amounts of
and reasons for significant transfers between Level&#160;1 and Level&#160;2, the
reasons for any transfers into or out of Level&#160;3, and information about
recurring Level&#160;3 measurements of purchases, sales, issuances and
settlements on a gross basis.&#160;&#160;The update also clarifies that entities
must provide (a)&#160;fair value measurement disclosures for each class of
assets and liabilities and (b)&#160;information about both the valuation
techniques and inputs used in estimating Level&#160;2 and Level&#160;3 fair
value measurements.&#160;&#160;We have applied the effective provisions of this
accounting standards update in preparing the disclosures in our notes to
condensed consolidated financial statements and our adoption did not have a
material effect on such disclosures.&#160;&#160;See Note&#160;2&#8212;Significant
Accounting Policies.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Subsequent events</font>&#8212;Effective
for financial statements issued after February&#160;2010, we adopted the
accounting standards update regarding subsequent events, which clarifies that
SEC filers are not required to disclose the date through which management
evaluated subsequent events in the financial statements.&#160;&#160;Our adoption
did not have a material effect on the disclosures contained within our notes to
condensed consolidated financial statements.&#160;&#160;See
Note&#160;2&#8212;Significant Accounting Policies.</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">Recently
Issued Accounting Standards</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Fair value measurements and
disclosures</font>&#8212;Effective January&#160;1, 2011, we will adopt the remaining
provisions of the accounting standards update that clarifies existing disclosure
requirements and<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>introduces additional
disclosure requirements for fair value measurements.&#160;&#160;The update
requires entities to separately disclose information about purchases, sales,
issuances, and settlements in the reconciliation of recurring Level&#160;3
measurements on a gross basis.&#160;&#160;The update is effective for interim
and annual periods beginning after December&#160;15, 2010.&#160;&#160;We do not
expect that our adoption will have a material effect on the disclosures
contained in our notes to consolidated financial statements.</font></div>

Interest Entities</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">TPDI and
ADDCL, two joint venture companies in which we hold interests, were formed to
own and operate certain ultra-deepwater drillships.&#160;&#160;We have
determined that each of these joint venture companies meets the criteria of a
variable interest entity for accounting purposes because their equity at risk is
insufficient to permit them to carry on their activities without additional
subordinated financial support from us.&#160;&#160;We have also determined, in
each case, that we are the primary beneficiary for accounting purposes since
(a)&#160;we have the power to direct the construction, marketing, and operating
activities, which are the activities that most significantly impact each
entity&#8217;s economic performance, and (b)&#160;we have the obligation to absorb a
majority of the losses or receive a majority of the benefits that could be
potentially significant to the variable interest entity.&#160;&#160;As a result,
we consolidate TPDI and ADDCL in our condensed consolidated financial
statements, we eliminate intercompany transactions, and we present the interests
that are not owned by us as noncontrolling interest on our condensed
consolidated balance sheets.&#160;&#160;The carrying amounts associated with
these two joint ventures, after eliminating the effect of intercompany
transactions, were as follows (in&#160;millions):</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 11pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">Note&#160;5&#8212;Impairments</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">During the
three months ended March&#160;31, 2010, we recognized a $2 million loss on
impairment of goodwill associated with our oil and gas properties.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">During the
three months ended March&#160;31, 2009, we determined that <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">GSF</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">&#160;</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Arctic</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">&#160;</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">II</font> and <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">GSF</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">&#160;</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Arctic</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">&#160;</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">IV</font>, both previously
classified as assets held for sale, were impaired due to the global economic
downturn and pressure on commodity prices, both of which have had an adverse
effect on our industry.&#160;&#160;We estimated the fair values of these rigs as
of the measurement date based on an exchange price that would be received for
the assets in the principal or most advantageous market for the assets in an
orderly transaction between market participants and considering our undertakings
to the Office of Fair Trading in the U.K. (&#8220;OFT&#8221;) that required the sale of the
rigs with certain limitations and in a limited amount of time.&#160;&#160;We
based our estimates on unobservable inputs that require significant judgment,
for which there is little or no market data, including non-binding price quotes
from unaffiliated parties with consideration of the then-current market
conditions and restrictions imposed by the OFT.&#160;&#160;As a result of our
evaluation, we recognized a loss on impairment of $221&#160;million
($0.69&#160;per diluted share), which had no tax effect, for the three months
ended March&#160;31, 2009.&#160;&#160;See Note&#160;8&#8212;Drilling Fleet Expansion
and Dispositions.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 11pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">Note&#160;6&#8212;Income
Taxes</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Overview</font>&#8212;Transocean&#160;Ltd.,
a holding company and Swiss resident, is exempt from cantonal and communal
income tax in Switzerland, but is subject to Swiss federal income
tax.&#160;&#160;At the federal level, qualifying net dividend income and net
capital gains on the sale of qualifying investments in subsidiaries are exempt
from Swiss federal income tax.&#160;&#160;Consequently, Transocean<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">&#160;</font>Ltd. expects
dividends from its subsidiaries and capital gains from sales of investments in
its subsidiaries to be exempt from Swiss federal income tax.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Tax provision</font>&#8212;We conduct
operations through our various subsidiaries in a number of countries throughout
the world, all of which have taxation regimes with varying nominal rates,
deductions, credits and other tax attributes.&#160;&#160;Our provision for
income taxes is based on the tax laws and rates applicable in the jurisdictions
in which we operate and earn income.&#160;&#160;Consequently, there is little to
no expected relationship between the provision for or benefit from income taxes
and income or loss before income taxes.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">Our
estimated annual effective tax rates for the three months ended March&#160;31,
2010 and March&#160;31, 2009 were 15.0&#160;percent and 15.2<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">&#160;</font>percent,
respectively.&#160;&#160;These rates were based on estimated annual income
before income taxes for each period after adjusting for certain items, such as
impairment losses and various other discrete items.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

valuation allowance for deferred tax assets, including those resulting from net
operating losses, when it is more likely than not that we will not realize some
or all of the benefit from the deferred tax assets.&#160;&#160;At March&#160;31,
2010 and December&#160;31, 2009, the valuation allowance for non-current
deferred tax assets was $69&#160;million.</font></div>

and local tax returns in several jurisdictions throughout the
world.&#160;&#160;With few exceptions, we are no longer subject to examinations
of our U.S. and non-U.S. tax matters for years prior to 1999.&#160;&#160;For the
three months ended March&#160;31, 2010 and March&#160;31, 2009, the amount of
current tax benefit recognized from the settlement of disputes with tax
authorities and from the expiration of statutes of limitations was
insignificant.</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">Our tax
returns in the other major jurisdictions in which we operate are generally
subject to examination for periods ranging from three to six
years.&#160;&#160;We have agreed to extensions beyond the statute of limitations
in three&#160;major jurisdictions for up to 15&#160;years.&#160;&#160;Tax
authorities in certain jurisdictions are examining our tax returns and in some
cases have issued assessments.&#160;&#160;We are defending our tax positions in
those jurisdictions.&#160;&#160;While we cannot predict or provide assurance as
to the final outcome of these proceedings, we do not expect the ultimate
liability to have a material adverse effect on our consolidated statement of
financial position or results of operations, although it may have a material
adverse effect on our consolidated cash flows.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Tax positions</font>&#8212;With respect to
our 2004 and 2005 U.S. federal income tax returns, the U.S. tax authorities have
withdrawn all of their previously proposed tax adjustments, except a claim
regarding transfer pricing for certain charters of drilling rigs between our
subsidiaries, reducing the total proposed adjustment to approximately
$79&#160;million, exclusive of interest.&#160;&#160;We believe an unfavorable
outcome on this assessment with respect to 2004 and 2005 activities would not
result in a material adverse effect on our consolidated financial position,
results of operations or cash flows.&#160;&#160;Although we believe the transfer
pricing for these charters is materially correct, we have been unable to reach a
resolution with the tax authorities and we expect the matter to proceed to
litigation.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">With respect
to the 2006 and 2007 U.S. federal income tax returns, we have been notified by
the U.S. tax authorities of proposed adjustments related to a series of
restructuring transactions that occurred between 2001 and 2004.&#160;&#160;These
restructuring transactions ultimately resulted in the disposition of our
interests in our former subsidiary TODCO in 2004 and 2005.&#160;&#160;The
authorities are disputing the amount of capital losses resulting from the
disposition of TODCO.&#160;&#160;We utilized a portion of the capital losses to
offset capital gains on our 2006, 2007, 2008 and 2009 tax
returns.&#160;&#160;The majority of the capital losses expired on
December&#160;31, 2009.&#160;&#160;The adjustments would also impact the amount
of certain net operating losses and other carryovers into 2006 and later
years.&#160;&#160;The proposed net adjustments to our 2006 and 2007 U.S. federal
income tax returns total approximately $188&#160;million.&#160;&#160;We believe
an unfavorable outcome on these proposed adjustments could result in a material
adverse effect on our consolidated financial position, results of operations or
cash flows.&#160;&#160;We believe that our tax returns are materially correct as
filed, and we will vigorously defend against any potential claims.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">Norwegian
civil tax and criminal authorities are investigating various transactions
undertaken by our subsidiaries in 2001 and 2002 as well as the actions of
certain of our former external advisors on these transactions.&#160;&#160;The
authorities issued tax assessments of approximately $263&#160;million, plus
interest, related to certain restructuring transactions, approximately $115<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">&#160;</font>million, plus
interest, related to the migration of a subsidiary that was previously subject
to tax in Norway, approximately $69<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">&#160;</font>million, plus
interest, related to a 2001 dividend payment, and approximately $8<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">&#160;</font>million, plus
interest, related to certain foreign exchange deductions and dividend
withholding tax.&#160;&#160;We have filed or expect to file appeals to all these
tax assessments.&#160;&#160;We may be required to provide some form of financial
security, in an amount up to $973<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">&#160;</font>million,
including interest and penalties, for these assessed amounts as this dispute is
appealed and addressed by the Norwegian courts.&#160;&#160;The authorities have
indicated that they plan to seek penalties of 60&#160;percent on all
matters.&#160;&#160;We believe an unfavorable outcome on these matters could
result in a material adverse effect on our consolidated financial position,
results of operations or cash flows.&#160; We believe our returns are materially
correct as filed, and we have and will continue to respond to all information
requests from the Norwegian authorities.&#160;&#160;We plan to vigorously
contest any assertions by the Norwegian authorities in connection with the
various transactions being investigated.</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">During the
three months ended March&#160;31, 2010, our long-term liability for unrecognized
tax benefits related to these Norwegian tax issues remained at $181&#160;million
due to the accrual of interest being offset by favorable exchange rate
fluctuations.&#160;&#160;While we cannot predict or provide assurance as to the
final outcome of these proceedings, we do not expect the ultimate resolution of
these matters to have a material adverse effect on our consolidated financial
position or results of operations, although it may have a material adverse
effect on our consolidated cash flows.</font></div>

our Brazilian income tax returns for the years 2000 through 2004 are currently
under examination.&#160;&#160;The Brazilian tax authorities have issued tax
assessments totaling $110&#160;million, plus a 75&#160;percent penalty of
$83&#160;million and $99&#160;million of interest through March&#160;31,
2010.&#160;&#160;We believe an unfavorable outcome on these
proposed&#160;assessments could result in a material adverse effect on our
consolidated financial position, results of operations or cash
flows.&#160;&#160;We believe our returns are materially correct as filed, and we
are vigorously contesting these assessments.&#160;&#160;We filed a protest
letter with the Brazilian tax authorities on January&#160;25, 2008, and we are
currently engaged in the appeals process.</font></div>

months ended March&#160;31, 2010, we completed the sale of two Midwater
Floaters, <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">GSF&#160;Arctic&#160;II</font> and
<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">GSF&#160;Arctic&#160;IV.</font>&#160;&#160;In
connection with the sale, we received net cash proceeds of $38&#160;million and
non-cash proceeds in the form of two notes receivable in the aggregate amount of
$165&#160;million.&#160;&#160;The notes receivable, which are secured by the
drilling units, have stated interest rates of 9&#160;percent and are payable in
scheduled quarterly installments of principal and interest through maturity in
January&#160;2015.&#160;&#160;We estimated the fair values of the notes
receivable based on unobservable inputs that require significant judgment, for
which there is little or no market data.&#160;&#160;We continue to operate <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">GSF&#160;Arctic&#160;IV</font> under
a short-term bareboat charter with the new owner of the vessel through
October&#160;2010.&#160;&#160;As a result of the sale, we recognized a loss on
disposal of assets for the three months ended March&#160;31, 2010 in the amount
of $15&#160;million.</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Commercial paper program</font>&#8212;We
maintain a commercial paper program, which is supported by the Five-Year
Revolving Credit Facility, under which we may issue privately placed, unsecured
commercial paper notes for general corporate purposes up to a maximum aggregate
outstanding amount of $1.5<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">&#160;</font>billion.&#160;&#160;At
March&#160;31, 2010, $150&#160;million in commercial paper was outstanding at a
weighted-average interest rate of 0.3<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">&#160;</font>percent.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Five-Year Revolving Credit
Facility</font>&#8212;We have a $2.0<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">&#160;</font>billion,
five-year revolving credit facility under the Five-Year Revolving Credit
Facility Agreement dated November&#160;27, 2007, as amended (the &#8220;Five-Year
Revolving Credit Facility&#8221;).&#160;&#160;Throughout the term of the Five-Year
Revolving Credit Facility, we pay a facility fee on the daily amount of the
underlying commitment, whether used or unused, which ranges from
0.10&#160;percent to 0.30&#160;percent and was 0.15&#160;percent at
March&#160;31, 2010.&#160;&#160;At March&#160;31, 2010, we had $81&#160;million
in letters of credit issued and outstanding and no borrowings outstanding under
the Five-Year Revolving Credit Facility.</font></div>

$2&#160;million associated with the debt component of the

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 11pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">Note&#160;10&#8212;Derivatives
and Hedging</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Cash flow hedges</font>&#8212;TPDI has
entered into interest rate swaps, which have been designated and have qualified
as a cash flow hedge, to reduce the variability of cash interest payments
associated with the variable-rate borrowings under the TPDI Credit
Facilities.&#160;&#160;The notional value increased proportionately with the
projected borrowings under the TPDI Credit Facilities to a maximum amount of
$1.190&#160;billion, of which $595&#160;million is attributable to one of our
subsidiaries.&#160;&#160;As of March&#160;31, 2010, the aggregate notional value
had increased to the maximum amount and the intercompany balances attributable
to our subsidiary have been eliminated in consolidation.&#160;&#160;Under the
interest rate swaps, TPDI receives interest at three-month London Interbank
Offered Rate and pays interest at a weighted-average fixed rate of 2.3<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">&#160;</font>percent during
the expected term of the TPDI Credit Facilities.&#160;&#160;At March&#160;31,
2010, the interest rate swaps represented a liability measured at fair value of
$2&#160;million, recorded in other long-term liabilities, with a corresponding
increase to accumulated other comprehensive loss.&#160;&#160;The
weighted-average variable interest rate on March&#160;31, 2010 was
3.9&#160;percent.&#160;&#160;At December&#160;31, 2009, the interest rate swaps
represented an asset measured at a fair value of $5&#160;million, recorded in
other assets, and a liability measured at fair value of less than
$1&#160;million, recorded in other long-term liabilities, with a corresponding
decrease to accumulated other comprehensive loss on our consolidated balance
sheet.&#160;&#160;The ineffective portion of the cash flow hedges was less than
$1&#160;million recorded in interest expense for the three months ended
March&#160;31, 2010.&#160;&#160;There was no ineffectiveness for the three
months ended March&#160;31, 2009.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Fair value hedges</font>&#8212;Two of our
wholly owned subsidiaries have entered into interest rate swaps, which are
designated and have qualified as fair value hedges, to reduce our exposure to
changes in the fair values of the 5.25%&#160;Senior Notes and the
5.00%&#160;Notes.&#160;&#160;The interest rate swaps have aggregate notional
values of $500&#160;million and $250&#160;million, respectively, equal to the
face values of the hedged instruments and have stated maturities that coincide
with those of the hedged instruments.&#160;&#160;We have determined that the
hedging relationships qualify for, and we have applied, the shortcut method of
accounting, under which the interest rate swaps are considered to have no
ineffectiveness and no ongoing assessment of effectiveness is
required.&#160;&#160;At March&#160;31, 2010, the interest rate swaps represented
an asset measured at fair value of $5&#160;million, recorded in other assets,
with a corresponding increase to the carrying amount of the underlying debt
instrument.&#160;&#160;The weighted-average variable interest rate on
March&#160;31, 2010 was 3.4&#160;percent.&#160;&#160;At December&#160;31, 2009,
the interest rate swaps represented a liability measured at a fair value of
$4&#160;million, recorded in other long-term liabilities, with a corresponding
decrease to the carrying amount of the underlying debt instrument.</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">Severance
plan</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">Following
our merger with GlobalSantaFe in 2007, we established a plan to consolidate
operations and administrative functions.&#160;&#160;As of March&#160;31, 2010,
we had identified 377&#160;employees who had been involuntarily terminated
pursuant to this plan.&#160;&#160;We recognized $5&#160;million and
$6&#160;million of severance expense in the three months ended March&#160;31,
2010 and March&#160;31, 2009, respectively, in either operating and maintenance
expense or general and administrative expense.&#160;&#160;The liability
associated with the severance plan, recorded in other current liabilities, was
$14&#160;million and $17&#160;million at March&#160;31, 2010 and
December&#160;31, 2009, respectively.&#160;&#160;Since the severance plan&#8217;s
inception in 2007, we have paid $61&#160;million in termination benefits under
the plan, including $8&#160;million and $4&#160;million paid during the three
months ended March&#160;31, 2010 and March&#160;31, 2009,
respectively.&#160;&#160;No additional amounts will be recognized under the
severance plan, which expired during the three months ended March&#160;31,
2010.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 11pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">Note&#160;12&#8212;Contingencies</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Legal</font> <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">proceedings</font></font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Asbestos litigation</font>&#8212;In 2004,
several of our subsidiaries were named, along with numerous other unaffiliated
defendants, in 21&#160;complaints filed on behalf of 769&#160;plaintiffs in the
Circuit Courts of the State of Mississippi and which claimed injuries arising
out of exposure to asbestos allegedly contained in drilling mud during these
plaintiffs&#8217; employment in drilling activities between 1965 and
1986.&#160;&#160;A Special Master, appointed to administer these cases
pre-trial, subsequently required that each individual plaintiff file a separate
lawsuit, and the original 21<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">&#160;</font>multi-plaintiff
complaints were then dismissed by the Circuit Courts.&#160;&#160;The amended
complaints resulted in one of our subsidiaries being named as a direct defendant
in seven cases.&#160;&#160;We have or may have an indirect interest in an
additional 17&#160;cases.&#160;&#160;The complaints generally allege that the
defendants used or manufactured asbestos-containing products in connection with
drilling operations and have included allegations of negligence, products
liability, strict liability and claims allowed under the Jones Act and general
maritime law.&#160;&#160;The plaintiffs generally seek awards of unspecified
compensatory and punitive damages.&#160;&#160;In each of these cases, the
complaints have named other unaffiliated defendant companies, including
companies that allegedly manufactured the drilling-related products that
contained asbestos.&#160;&#160;None of the cases in which one of our
subsidiaries is a named defendant has been scheduled for trial in 2010, and the
preliminary information available on these claims is not sufficient to determine
if there is an identifiable period for alleged exposure to asbestos, whether any
asbestos exposure in fact occurred, the vessels potentially involved in the
claims, or the basis on which the plaintiffs would support claims that their
injuries were related to exposure to asbestos.&#160;&#160;However, the initial
evidence available would suggest that we would have significant defenses to
liability and damages.&#160;&#160;In 2009, two cases that were part of the
original 2004 multi-plaintiff suits went to trial in Mississippi against
unaffiliated defendant companies which allegedly manufactured drilling-related
products containing asbestos.&#160;&#160;We were not a defendant in either of
these cases.&#160;&#160;One of the cases resulted in a substantial jury verdict
in favor of the plaintiff, and this verdict was subsequently vacated by the
trial judge on the basis that the plaintiff failed to meet its burden of
proof.&#160;&#160;While the court&#8217;s decision is consistent with our general
evaluation of the strength of these cases, it has not been reviewed on
appeal.&#160;&#160;The second case resulted in a verdict completely in favor of
the defendants.&#160;&#160;There have been no other trials involving any of the
parties to the original 21&#160;complaints.&#160;&#160;We intend to defend these
lawsuits vigorously, although there can be no assurance as to the ultimate
outcome.&#160;&#160;We historically have maintained broad liability insurance,
although we are not certain whether insurance will cover the liabilities, if
any, arising out of these claims.&#160;&#160;Based on our evaluation of the
exposure to date, we do not expect the liability, if any, resulting from these
claims to have a material adverse effect on our consolidated statement of
financial position, results of operations or cash flows.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">One of our
subsidiaries was involved in lawsuits arising out of the subsidiary&#8217;s
involvement in the design, construction and refurbishment of major industrial
complexes.&#160;&#160;The operating assets of the subsidiary were sold and its
operations discontinued in 1989, and the subsidiary has no remaining assets
other than the insurance policies involved in its litigation, fundings from
settlements with the primary insurers and funds received from the cancellation
of certain insurance policies.&#160;&#160;The subsidiary has been named as a
defendant, along with numerous other companies, in lawsuits alleging personal
injury as a result of exposure to asbestos.&#160;&#160;As of March&#160;31,
2010, the subsidiary was a defendant in approximately
1,054&#160;lawsuits.&#160;&#160;Some of these lawsuits include multiple
plaintiffs and we estimate that there are approximately 2,612&#160;plaintiffs in
these lawsuits.&#160;&#160;For many of these lawsuits, we have not been provided
with sufficient information from the plaintiffs to determine whether all or some
of the plaintiffs have claims against the subsidiary, the basis of any such
claims, or the nature of their alleged injuries.&#160;&#160;The first of the
asbestos-related lawsuits was filed against this subsidiary in
1990.&#160;&#160;Through March&#160;31,&#160;2010, the amounts expended to
resolve claims (including both attorneys&#8217; fees and expenses, and settlement
costs) have not been material, and all deductibles with respect to the primary
insurance have been satisfied.&#160;&#160;The subsidiary continues to be named
as a defendant in additional lawsuits and we cannot predict the number of
additional cases in which it may be named a defendant nor can we predict the
potential costs to resolve such additional cases or to resolve the pending
cases.&#160;&#160;However, the subsidiary has in excess of $1<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">&#160;</font>billion in
insurance limits potentially available to the subsidiary.&#160;&#160;Although
not all of the policies may be fully available due to the insolvency of certain
insurers, we believe that the subsidiary will have sufficient insurance and
funds from the settlements of litigation with insurance carriers available to
respond to these claims.&#160;&#160;While we cannot predict or provide assurance
as to the final outcome of these matters, we do not believe that the current
value of the claims where we have been identified will have a material impact on
our consolidated statement of financial position, results of operations or cash
flows.</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Rio de Janeiro tax
assessment</font>&#8212;In the third quarter of 2006, we received tax assessments of
approximately $164&#160;million from the state tax authorities of Rio de Janeiro
in Brazil against one of our Brazilian subsidiaries for taxes on equipment
imported into the state in connection with our operations.&#160;&#160;The
assessments resulted from a preliminary finding by these authorities that our
subsidiary&#8217;s record keeping practices were deficient.&#160;&#160;We currently
believe that the substantial majority of these assessments are without
merit.&#160;&#160;We filed an initial response with the Rio de Janeiro tax
authorities on September&#160;9, 2006 refuting these additional tax
assessments.&#160;&#160;In September&#160;2007, we received confirmation from
the state tax authorities that they believe the additional tax assessments are
valid, and as a result, we filed an appeal on September&#160;27, 2007 to the
state Taxpayer&#8217;s Council contesting these assessments.&#160;&#160;While we
cannot predict or provide assurance as to the final outcome of these
proceedings, we do not expect it to have a material adverse effect on our
consolidated statement of financial position, results of operations or cash
flows.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Patent Litigation</font>&#8212;Several of
our subsidiaries have been sued by Heerema Engineering Services (&#8220;Heerema&#8221;) in
the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Texas for patent
infringement, claiming that we infringe their U.S. patent entitled Method and
Device for Drilling Oil and Gas.&#160;&#160;Heerema claims that our Enterprise
class, advanced Enterprise class, Express class and Development Driller class of
drilling rigs operating in the U.S. Gulf of Mexico infringe on this
patent.&#160;&#160;They seek unspecified damages and injunctive
relief.&#160;&#160;The court has held a hearing on construction of their patent
but has not yet issued a decision.&#160;&#160;We deny liability for patent
infringement, believe that their patent is invalid and intend to vigorously
defend against the claim.&#160;&#160;We do not expect the liability, if any,
resulting from this claim to have a material adverse effect on our consolidated
statement of financial position, results of operations or cash
flows.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Other matters</font>&#8212;We are involved
in various tax matters and various regulatory matters.&#160;&#160;We are also
involved in lawsuits relating to damage claims arising out of hurricanes Katrina
and Rita, all of which are insured and which are not material to
us.&#160;&#160;In addition, as of March&#160;31, 2010, we were involved in a
number of other lawsuits, including a dispute for municipal tax payments in
Brazil and a dispute involving customs procedures in India, neither of which is
material to us, and all of which have arisen in the ordinary course of our
business.&#160;&#160;We do not expect the liability, if any, resulting from
these other matters to have a material adverse effect on our consolidated
statement of financial position, results of operations or cash
flows.&#160;&#160;We cannot predict with certainty the outcome or effect of any
of the litigation matters specifically described above or of any such other
pending or threatened litigation.&#160;&#160;There can be no assurance that our
beliefs or expectations as to the outcome or effect of any lawsuit or other
litigation matter will prove correct and the eventual outcome of these matters
could materially differ from management&#8217;s current estimates.&#160;&#160;See
Note&#160;15&#8212;Subsequent Events.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">Environmental
matters</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">We have
certain potential liabilities under the Comprehensive Environmental Response,
Compensation and Liability Act (&#8220;CERCLA&#8221;) and similar state acts regulating
cleanup of various hazardous waste disposal sites, including those described
below.&#160;&#160;CERCLA is intended to expedite the remediation of hazardous
substances without regard to fault.&#160;&#160;Potentially responsible parties
(&#8220;PRPs&#8221;) for each site include present and former owners and operators of,
transporters to and generators of the substances at the
site.&#160;&#160;Liability is strict and can be joint and several.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">We have been
named as a PRP in connection with a site located in Santa&#160;Fe Springs,
California, known as the Waste Disposal,<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">&#160;</font>Inc.
site.&#160;&#160;We and other PRPs have agreed with the U.S. Environmental
Protection Agency (&#8220;EPA&#8221;) and the U.S. Department of Justice (&#8220;DOJ&#8221;) to settle
our potential liabilities for this site by agreeing to perform the remaining
remediation required by the EPA.&#160;&#160;The form of the agreement is a
consent decree, which has been entered by the court.&#160;&#160;The parties to
the settlement have entered into a participation agreement, which makes us
liable for approximately eight&#160;percent of the remediation and related
costs.&#160;&#160;The remediation is complete, and we believe our share of the
future operation and maintenance costs of the site is not
material.&#160;&#160;There are additional potential liabilities related to the
site, but these cannot be quantified, and we have no reason at this time to
believe that they will be material.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">One of our
subsidiaries has been ordered by the California Regional Water Quality Control
Board (&#8220;CRWQCB&#8221;) to develop a testing plan for a site known as Campus 1000
Fremont in Alhambra, California.&#160;&#160;This site was formerly owned and
operated by certain of our subsidiaries.&#160;&#160;It is presently owned by an
unrelated party, which has received an order to test the property.&#160;&#160;We
have also been advised that one or more of our subsidiaries is likely to be
named by the EPA as a PRP for the San Gabriel Valley, Area&#160;3, Superfund
site, which includes this property.&#160;&#160;Testing has been completed at the
property but no contaminants of concern were detected.&#160;&#160;In discussions
with CRWQCB staff we were advised of their intent to issue us a &#8220;no further
action&#8221; letter but it has not yet been received.&#160;&#160;Based on the test
results, we would contest any potential liability.&#160;&#160;We have no
knowledge at this time of the potential cost of any remediation, who else will
be named as PRPs, and whether in fact any of our subsidiaries is a responsible
party.&#160;&#160;The subsidiaries in question do not own any operating assets
and have limited ability to respond to any liabilities.</font></div>

of other claims by the EPA, the involved state agency or PRPs are at various
stages of investigation.&#160;&#160;These investigations involve determinations

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">It is
difficult to quantify with certainty the potential cost of these environmental
matters, particularly in respect of remediation
obligations.&#160;&#160;Nevertheless, based upon the information currently
available, we believe that our ultimate liability arising from all environmental
matters, including the liability for all other related pending legal
proceedings, asserted legal claims and known potential legal claims which are
likely to be asserted, is adequately accrued and should not have a material
effect on our financial position or ongoing results of
operations.&#160;&#160;Estimated costs of future expenditures for environmental
remediation obligations are not discounted to their present value.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">Contamination
litigation</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">On
July&#160;11, 2005, one of our subsidiaries was served with a lawsuit filed on
behalf of three landowners in Louisiana in the 12<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">th</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">&#160;</font>Judicial
District Court for the Parish of Avoyelles, State of Louisiana.&#160;&#160;The
lawsuit named nineteen other defendants, all of which were alleged to have
contaminated the plaintiffs&#8217; property with naturally occurring radioactive
material, produced water, drilling fluids, chlorides, hydrocarbons, heavy metals
and other contaminants as a result of oil and gas exploration
activities.&#160;&#160;Experts retained by the plaintiffs issued a report
suggesting significant contamination in the area operated by the subsidiary and
another codefendant, and claimed that over $300<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">&#160;</font>million would be
required to properly remediate the contamination.&#160;&#160;The experts
retained by the defendants conducted their own investigation and concluded that
the remediation costs would amount to no more than $2.5<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">&#160;</font>million.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">The
plaintiffs and the codefendant threatened to add GlobalSantaFe as a defendant in
the lawsuit under the &#8220;single business enterprise&#8221; doctrine contained in
Louisiana law.&#160;&#160;The single business enterprise doctrine is similar to
corporate veil piercing doctrines.&#160;&#160;On August&#160;16, 2006, our
subsidiary and its immediate parent company, each of which is an entity that no
longer conducts operations or holds assets, filed voluntary petitions for relief
under Chapter&#160;11 of the U.S. Bankruptcy Code in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court
for the District of Delaware.&#160;&#160;Later that day, the plaintiffs
dismissed our subsidiary from the lawsuit.&#160;&#160;Subsequently, the
codefendant filed various motions in the lawsuit and in the Delaware
bankruptcies attempting to assert alter ego and single business enterprise
claims against GlobalSantaFe and two other subsidiaries in the
lawsuit.&#160;&#160;The efforts to assert alter ego and single business
enterprise theory claims against GlobalSantaFe were rejected by the Court in
Avoyelles Parish, and the lawsuit against the other defendant went to trial on
February&#160;19, 2007.&#160;&#160;This lawsuit was resolved at trial with a
settlement by the codefendant that included a $20<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">&#160;</font>million payment
and certain cleanup activities to be conducted by the codefendant.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">The
codefendant sought to dismiss the bankruptcies.&#160;&#160;In addition, the
codefendant filed proofs of claim against both our subsidiary and its parent
with regard to its claims arising out of the settlement of the
lawsuit.&#160;&#160;On February&#160;15, 2008, the Bankruptcy Court denied the
codefendant&#8217;s request to dismiss the bankruptcy case but modified the automatic
stay to allow the codefendant to proceed on its claims against the debtors, our
subsidiary and its parent, and their insurance companies.&#160;&#160;The
codefendant subsequently filed suit against the debtors and certain of its
insurers in the Court of Avoyelles Parish to determine their liability for the
settlement.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">The
codefendant filed a Notice of Appeal of the rulings of the Bankruptcy
Court.&#160;&#160;GlobalSantaFe and its two subsidiaries also filed Notices of
Appeal to the U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware.&#160;&#160;On
January&#160;27, 2009, the codefendant&#8217;s appeal was granted by the District
Court and the bankruptcy case was remanded to the Bankruptcy Court with
instructions to have the case dismissed.&#160;&#160;On February&#160;10, 2009,
the Bankruptcy Court entered an order dismissing the bankruptcy
case.&#160;&#160;The debtors, GlobalSantaFe and the two subsidiaries have filed
Notices of Appeal of the District Court&#8217;s ruling with the U.S. Court of Appeals
for the Third Circuit.&#160;&#160;On February&#160;18, 2009, the District Court
stayed its ruling which instructed the Bankruptcy Court to dismiss the
case.&#160;&#160;The appeal was heard on September&#160;14, 2009.&#160;&#160;On
December&#160;22, 2009, the Court of Appeals affirmed the ruling of the District
Court.&#160;&#160;On January&#160;5, 2010, we petitioned the Third Circuit for a
rehearing of that ruling.&#160;&#160;On January&#160;27, 2010, the Third Circuit
declined the petitions for rehearing and on February&#160;4, 2010, the Third
Circuit issued its mandate and the District Court responded by closing the
appeal pending in the District Court the same day.&#160;&#160;The matter was
then referred to the Bankruptcy Court for dismissal.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">On
February&#160;1, 2010, the codefendant filed a motion for sanctions against the
debtors, GlobalSantaFe and the two subsidiaries and counsel for all the
companies based on the dismissal of the bankruptcy cases.&#160;&#160;Thereafter
on February&#160;12, 2010, the codefendant filed a motion to vacate the
automatic stay.&#160;&#160;On March&#160;10, 2010, a hearing was conducted in
the Bankruptcy Court on the above motions.&#160;&#160;The motion for sanctions
was taken under advisement by the Bankruptcy Court and, on the same day, the
Bankruptcy Court entered an order vacating the automatic stay in the Bankruptcy
Case in its entirety.&#160;&#160;The Bankruptcy Case remains open subject to the
mandate and the pending motion for sanctions.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">After entry
of the order vacating the automatic stay, GlobalSantaFe and the two subsidiaries
filed a declaratory judgment action in State District Court in Houston, Texas
against the codefendant and the debtors seeking a declaration that GlobalSantaFe
and the two subsidiaries had no liability under legal theories advanced by the
codefendant.&#160;&#160;On March&#160;11, 2010, the codefendant filed a motion
for leave to amend the pending litigation in Avoyelles Parish to add
GlobalSantaFe, Transocean Worldwide Inc., its successor and our wholly owned
subsidiary, and one of the subsidiaries as well as various additional
insurers.&#160;&#160;Leave to amend was granted and the amended petition was
filed.&#160;&#160;An extension to respond for all purposes was agreed until
April&#160;28, 2010 for the debtors, GlobalSantaFe, Transocean Worldwide Inc.
and the subsidiary.</font></div>

              <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 11pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">TRANSOCEAN
