              <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 11pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">NOTES
TO CONDENSED CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (Continued)</font></div>
              <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">(Unaudited)</font></div>
              <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
            </div>
          </div>
        </div><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">We believe
that these legal theories should not be applied against GlobalSantaFe or
Transocean Worldwide Inc.&#160;&#160;Our subsidiary, its parent and
GlobalSantaFe intend to continue to vigorously defend against any action taken
in an attempt to impose liability against them under the theories discussed
above or otherwise and believe they have good and valid defenses
thereto.&#160;&#160;We do not believe that these claims will have a material
impact on our consolidated statement of financial position, results of
operations or cash flows.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">Retained
risk</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">Our
insurance program consisted of commercial market and captive insurance policies
primarily with 12 month policy periods beginning on May 1, 2009. Under the
program, we generally maintain a $125 million per occurrence deductible, limited
to a maximum of $250 million per year, on our hull and machinery. However, in
the event of a total loss or a constructive total loss of a drilling unit, such
loss would be subject to a deductible ranging from $0.5 million to $1.5 million.
Subject to the same shared deductible, we also have coverage for costs incurred
to mitigate damage to a rig&#160;up to&#160;an amount equal to 25 percent of a
rig&#8217;s insured value. Also subject to the same shared deductible, we have
coverage for wreck removal for up to 25 percent of a rig&#8217;s insured value, with
any excess generally covered to the extent of our excess liability coverage
described below.&#160;&#160;We carry $950 million of commercial market excess
liability coverage, exclusive of deductibles and self-insured retention, noted
below, which generally covers offshore risks such as personal injury,
third-party property claims, and third-party non-crew claims, including wreck
removal and pollution.&#160;&#160;Our excess liability coverage has separate (1)
$10 million per occurrence deductibles&#160;on crew personal injury liability
and on collision liability claims and (2) a separate $5 million per occurrence
deductible on&#160;other third-party non-crew claims. These types of excess
liability coverages are subject to an additional aggregate&#160;self-insured
retention&#160;of $50 million that is applied to any occurrence in excess of the
per occurrence deductible until the $50 million is exhausted.&#160;&#160;We
generally retain the risk for any liability losses in excess
of&#160;$1.0&#160;billion.&#160;&#160;We also carry $100 million of additional
insurance that generally covers expenses that would otherwise be assumed by the
well owner, such as costs to control the well, redrill expenses and pollution
from the well.&#160;&#160;This additional insurance provides coverage for such
expenses in circumstances in which we have legal or contractual liability
arising from our gross negligence and/or willful misconduct.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">We have
elected to self-insure operators extra expense coverage for ADTI and
CMI.&#160;&#160;This coverage provides protection against expenses related to
well control, pollution&#160;and redrill liability associated with
blowouts.&#160;&#160;Generally, ADTI&#8217;s customers assume, and indemnify ADTI for,
liability associated with blowouts in excess of $50 million.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">As of March
31, 2010, the insured value of our drilling rig fleet was approximately $39
billion in the aggregate.&#160;&#160;See Note 15&#8212;Subsequent Events.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">We generally
do not have commercial market insurance coverage for physical damage losses,
including liability for wreck removal expenses, to our fleet caused by named
windstorms in the U.S. Gulf of Mexico and war perils worldwide. Except with
respect to <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Dhirubhai Deepwater
KG1</font> and <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Dhirubhai
Deepwater KG2</font>, we generally do not carry insurance for loss of revenue
unless contractually required.</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">Letters
of credit and surety bonds</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">We had
letters of credit outstanding totaling $500&#160;million and $567&#160;million
at March&#160;31, 2010 and December&#160;31, 2009,
respectively.&#160;&#160;These letters of credit guarantee various contract
bidding and performance activities under various committed and uncommitted
credit lines provided by several banks.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">As is

Value of Financial Instruments</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">We estimate
the fair value of each class of financial instruments, for which estimating fair
value is practicable, by applying the following methods and
assumptions:</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Cash and cash equivalents</font>&#8212;The
carrying amount approximates fair value because of the short maturities of those
instruments.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Accounts receivable</font>&#8212;The
carrying amount, net of valuation allowance, approximates fair value because of
the short maturities of those instruments.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Short-term investments</font>&#8212;The
carrying amount represents the estimated fair value, measured using pricing data
that are representative of quoted prices for similar instruments in active
markets or identical instruments in less active markets.&#160;&#160;Our
short-term investments include investments in The Reserve International
Liquidity Fund Ltd. and The Reserve Primary Fund.&#160;&#160;At March&#160;31,
2010 and December&#160;31, 2009, the carrying amount of our short-term
investments was $32&#160;million and $38&#160;million, respectively, recorded in
other assets on our condensed consolidated balance sheets.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Notes receivable</font>&#8212;The carrying
amount represents the estimated fair value, measured using unobservable inputs
that require significant judgment, for which there is little or no market
data.&#160;&#160;At March&#160;31, 2010, the aggregate carrying amount of our
notes receivable was $130&#160;million, including $19&#160;million and
$111&#160;million recorded in other current assets and other assets,
respectively.&#160;&#160;We did not hold notes receivable as of
December&#160;31, 2009.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Debt</font>&#8212;The fair value of our
fixed-rate debt is measured using quoted prices for identical instruments in
active markets.&#160;&#160;Our variable-rate debt is included in the fair values
stated below at its carrying amount since the short-term interest rates cause

Overseas Drilling Limited Loan Facility are included in the fair values stated
below at their aggregate carrying amount of $158&#160;million at March&#160;31,
2010 and December&#160;31, 2009, since there is no available market price for
such related-party debt.&#160;&#160;The carrying amounts and estimated fair
values of our long-term debt, including debt due within one year, were as
follows (in&#160;millions):</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Share repurchase
program</font>&#8212;Subsequent to March&#160;31, 2010, we repurchased 1,732,900 of
our shares under our share repurchase program in exchange for an aggregate
amount of CHF&#160;160&#160;million, equivalent to
$150&#160;million.&#160;&#160;At May&#160;5, 2010, we held
2,449,900&#160;treasury shares, at cost.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Deepwater
Horizon</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">
incident</font>&#8212;Subsequent to March&#160;31, 2010, our Ultra-Deepwater Floater
<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Deepwater&#160;Horizon</font>,
which had been drilling a well for its operator in the U.S. Gulf of Mexico, sank
on April&#160;22, 2010 after an explosion and fire onboard the rig that began on
April&#160;20, 2010.&#160;&#160;Eleven persons are missing and presumed dead and
others were injured as a result of the incident.&#160;&#160;Our underwriters
declared the vessel a total loss and, as of May 5, 2010, we&#160;received $401
million as partial payment of the expected insurance recoveries.&#160; The
combined response team was unable to stem the flow of hydrocarbons from the well
prior to the sinking of the rig and&#160;efforts to contain the flow of
hydrocarbons are still underway.&#160;&#160;The Departments of Homeland Security
and Interior have begun a joint investigation into the cause of the
incident.&#160;&#160;The U.S. Coast Guard and the Minerals Management Service
share jurisdiction over the investigation into the incident.&#160;&#160;In
addition, various committees and subcommittees of the&#160;House of
Representatives and the Senate of the United States have requested our
participation in hearings related to the incident.&#160;&#160;We have also
received a request to preserve information from the DOJ.&#160; There have also
been numerous lawsuits filed related to the incident, and we expect additional
lawsuits to be filed.&#160;&#160;We expect to incur significant legal fees and
costs in responding to these matters.</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">Transocean&#160;Ltd.

otherwise, &#8220;Transocean,&#8221; the &#8220;Company,&#8221; &#8220;we,&#8221; &#8220;us&#8221; or &#8220;our&#8221;) is a leading
international provider of offshore contract drilling services for oil and gas
wells.&#160;&#160;As of April&#160;30, 2010, we owned, had partial ownership
interests in or operated 139<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">&#160;</font>mobile offshore
drilling units.&#160;&#160;As of this date, our fleet consisted of 45<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">&#160;</font>High-Specification
Floaters (Ultra-Deepwater, Deepwater and Harsh Environment semisubmersibles and
drillships), 26<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">&#160;</font>Midwater
Floaters, 10&#160;High-Specification Jackups, 55<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">&#160;</font>Standard Jackups
and three<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">&#160;</font>Other
Rigs.&#160;&#160;In addition, we had three<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">&#160;</font>Ultra-Deepwater
Floaters under construction.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">We operate
in two reportable segments: (1)&#160;contract drilling services and
(2)&#160;other operations.&#160;&#160;Contract drilling services, our primary
business, involves contracting our mobile offshore drilling fleet, related
equipment and work crews primarily on a dayrate basis to drill oil and gas
wells.&#160;&#160;We believe our drilling fleet is one of the most modern and
versatile fleets in the world, consisting of floaters, jackups and other rigs
used in support of offshore drilling activities and offshore support services on
a worldwide basis.&#160;&#160;We specialize in technically demanding regions of
the offshore drilling business with a particular focus on deepwater and harsh
environment drilling services.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">Our contract
drilling operations are geographically dispersed in oil and gas exploration and
development areas throughout the world.&#160;&#160;Although rigs can be moved
from one region to another, the cost of moving rigs and the availability of
rig-moving vessels may cause the supply and demand balance to fluctuate somewhat
between regions.&#160;&#160;Still, significant variations between regions do not
tend to persist long term because of rig mobility.&#160;&#160;Our fleet operates
in a single, global market for the provision of contract drilling
services.&#160;&#160;The location of our rigs and the allocation of resources to
build or upgrade rigs are determined by the activities and needs of our
customers.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">The other
operations segment includes drilling management services and oil and gas
properties.&#160;&#160;Drilling management services are provided through Applied
Drilling Technology&#160;Inc., our wholly owned subsidiary, and through ADT
International, a division of one of our U.K. subsidiaries (together,
&#8220;ADTI&#8221;).&#160;&#160;ADTI provides oil and gas drilling management services on
either a dayrate basis or a completed-project, fixed-price (or &#8220;turnkey&#8221;) basis,
as well as drilling engineering and drilling project management
services.&#160;&#160;Our oil and gas properties consist of exploration,
development and production activities carried out through Challenger
Minerals&#160;Inc. and Challenger Minerals (North Sea) Limited (together,
&#8220;CMI&#8221;), our oil and gas subsidiaries.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 11pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">Significant
Events</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Deepwater
Horizon</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">
incident</font>&#8212;On April&#160;22, 2010, the Ultra-Deepwater Floater <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Deepwater&#160;Horizon</font> sank
following a fire and explosion while operating in the U.S. Gulf of Mexico and
has been declared a total loss.&#160;&#160;Eleven persons are missing and
presumed dead and others were injured as a result of the incident.&#160;&#160;As
we continue to investigate the cause of the incident, we are evaluating its
consequences, which are expected to have a material effect on our future
consolidated results of operations and cash flows and may have a material effect
on our future consolidated statement of financial position.&#160;&#160;Although
the rig was operating under a contract which was to extend through
September&#160;2013, the total loss of the rig results in an automatic
termination of the agreement.&#160;&#160;The backlog associated with the
drilling contract under which <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Deepwater&#160;Horizon</font> was
operating was approximately $590&#160;million.&#160;&#160;The rig had an insured
value of $560&#160;million,&#160;subject to a deductible ranging from
$0.5&#160;million to $1.5&#160;million.&#160;&#160;As of&#160;May 5, 2010, we
have received $401 million as partial payment of the expected insurance
recoveries.&#160; We carry insurance that covers wreck removal, if
required,&#160;subject to certain limits and deductibles.&#160;&#160;We can
provide no assurances as to the estimated costs, insurance recoveries, or other
actions that will result from this incident.&#160;&#160;See &#8220;&#8212;Outlook&#8212;Insurance
matters,&#8221; &#8220;Part II.&#160; Other Information, Item 1.&#160; Legal Proceedings&#8221;
and &#8220;Part II.&#160;&#160;Other Information, Item&#160;1A. Risk
Factors.&#8221;</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Fleet expansion</font>&#8212;We have
recently completed construction of three&#160;Ultra-Deepwater newbuilds and each
has departed the shipyard.&#160;&#160;As of April&#160;13, 2010, two of these
units had been accepted by their respective customers and commenced their
respective contracts.&#160;&#160;See &#8220;&#8212;Outlook.&#8221;</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Exchange listing</font>&#8212;Effective
April&#160;20, 2010, our shares began trading on the SIX Swiss Exchange under
the symbol &#8220;RIGN.&#8221;&#160;&#160;Our shares also continue to be listed on the New
York Stock Exchange under the symbol &#8220;RIG.&#8221;</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Share repurchase program</font>&#8212;As of
May&#160;5, 2010, we had repurchased a total of 2,449,900 of our shares under
our share repurchase program in exchange for an aggregate amount of
CHF&#160;224&#160;million, equivalent to $210&#160;million.&#160;&#160;See
&#8220;&#8212;Liquidity and Capital Resources&#8212;Sources and Uses of Liquidity.&#8221;</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Dispositions</font>&#8212;During the three
months ended March&#160;31, 2010, we completed the sale of two Midwater
Floaters, <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">GSF&#160;Arctic&#160;II</font> and
<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">GSF&#160;Arctic&#160;IV</font>.&#160;&#160;In
connection with the sale, we received net cash proceeds of $38&#160;million and
non-cash proceeds in the form of two notes receivable in the aggregate amount of
$165&#160;million.&#160;&#160;As a result of the sale, we recognized a loss on
disposal of assets for the three months ended March&#160;31, 2010 in the amount
of $15&#160;million.&#160;&#160;See &#8220;&#8212;Liquidity and Capital Resources&#8212;Fleet
Expansion and Dispositions.&#8221;</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Drilling market</font>&#8212;We expect
market utilization to stabilize over the next few quarters, possibly at lower
levels than those of 2008, due to continued stability in oil and gas prices and
in the credit markets.&#160;&#160;Additionally, we expect this stability to
result in improved contracting opportunities for our High-Specification Floater
fleet during 2010.&#160;&#160;However, considering the uncontracted capacity in
2010 and 2011 from newbuilds and existing units in the market, we cannot be
certain of projections for utilization for our High-Specification Floater
fleet.&#160;&#160;Consequently, we do not believe that the increased tendering
activity that we are currently experiencing will foster a corresponding increase
in dayrates or a return to the highs experienced in 2008 in the near
term.&#160;&#160;See &#8220;Item&#160;1A. Risk Factors&#8221; in our annual report on Form
10-K for the year ended December&#160;31, 2009 for a discussion of some of the
risks associated with a possible decline in commodity prices and an extended
worldwide economic downturn.</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">As of
April&#160;13, 2010, our contract backlog had declined to $28.6&#160;billion, as
adjusted for the $590&#160;million lost backlog associated with the drilling
contract under which <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Deepwater
Horizon</font> was operating.&#160;&#160;As of February&#160;2, 2010, our
contract backlog was $30.4&#160;billion.&#160;&#160;Although we are currently
engaged in advanced discussions with customers on several additional
opportunities, our backlog may continue to decline if we are unable to obtain
new contracts for our rigs that sufficiently replace existing backlog as it is
consumed over time.</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">We have
14&#160;existing contracts with fixed-price or capped options, and given current
market conditions, we expect that a number of these options will not be
exercised by our customers in 2010.&#160;&#160;Well-in-progress or similar
provisions of our existing contracts may delay the start of higher dayrates in
subsequent contracts, and some of the delays could be significant.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">High-Specification
Floaters</font>&#8212;Our Ultra-Deepwater Floater fleet is fully contracted for 2010,
and we recently contracted an Ultra-Deepwater Floater available in 2011 for two
years.&#160;&#160;We recently extended a Deepwater Floater available in 2010 for
a three-year period and two other Deepwater Floaters, also available in 2010,
for seven months each.&#160;&#160;Recent subletting of our High-Specification
Floater fleet has had minimal impact on our operations in&#160;2010 thus far,
but we cannot be certain of the impact on our operations in&#160;2011 and
beyond.&#160;&#160;As of April&#160;13, 2010, after adjusting for the loss of
<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Deepwater&#160;Horizon,
</font>we had 44 of our 48<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">&#160;</font>current and
future High-Specification Floaters contracted through the end of 2010, with 32,
including all of our newbuilds, contracted beyond 2011.&#160;&#160;These
44&#160;units also include all of our Ultra-Deepwater Floaters.&#160;&#160;We
believe the continued exploration successes in the deepwater offshore provinces
will foster significant demand and should support our long-term positive outlook
for our High-Specification Floater fleet.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Midwater Floaters</font>&#8212;For our
Midwater Floater fleet, which includes 26<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">&#160;</font>semisubmersible
rigs, near-term customer interest has remained steady and in line with the
previous quarter.&#160;&#160;During the first quarter of 2010, active tendering
resulted in the execution of several contracts for our Midwater Floater fleet
and the reactivation of one stacked unit.&#160;&#160;Sixty-nine&#160;percent of
our Midwater Floater fleet is committed to contracts that extend into the second
quarter of 2010.&#160;&#160;We believe the recent increased tendering activity
could result in our active rigs working beyond their current contracts and the
possibility of reactivating one or more of our five stacked Midwater Floaters in
the second half of 2010.&#160;&#160;Market utilization for this fleet, however,
may face challenges from the moored Deepwater Floaters coming available in 2010
and potentially competing in the midwater market due to the lack of current
opportunities in the deepwater market.&#160;&#160;Tenders for our Midwater
Floaters are generally shorter in duration, resulting in these units working on
well-to-well programs.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">High-Specification Jackups
</font>and<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic"> Standard
Jackups&#8212;</font>Considering the number of units currently stacked, and the number
of newbuild units expected to enter the market without customer contracts and
the absence of a corresponding increase in customer demand, we expect near-term
dayrates for our jackup fleet to decline as contracts are renewed or
completed.&#160;&#160;However, tendering activity has increased during the first
quarter of 2010, which has resulted in new contracts, including the reactivation
of four stacked units, and extensions of several existing
contracts.&#160;&#160;As of April&#160;13, 2010, we had three&#160;of our 10
High-Specification Jackups and 20&#160;of our 55&#160;Standard Jackups
stacked.&#160;&#160;Although we have two&#160; High-Specification Jackups and
six&#160;Standard Jackups completing their current contracts in the
second&#160;quarter of 2010, the continued increase in tendering activity could
result in the extension of these contracts or the reactivation of a few of our
stacked units in the second half of 2010.</font></div>

                <div align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 9pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">Average
      daily revenue is defined as contract drilling revenue earned per revenue

      which a rig earns dayrate after commencement of
      operations.&#160;&#160;Stacking rigs, such as Midwater Floaters,
      High-Specification Jackups and Standard Jackups, has the effect of
      increasing the average daily revenue since these rig types are typically
      contracted at lower dayrates compared to the High-Specification
      Floaters.</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">Resulting
from the market pressures experienced in the three months ended March&#160;31,
2010, our revenues declined relative to those recognized in the three months
ended March&#160;31, 2009.&#160;&#160;The decline was primarily due to lower
utilization, mostly related to 33<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">&#160;</font>stacked and idle
rigs as of March<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">&#160;</font>31, 2010, as
compared to six stacked rigs during the same period in 2009.&#160;&#160;This
decline was partially offset by revenues from the commencement of operations of
our newbuild rigs.&#160;&#160;The decreased utilization also resulted in a
decrease in our operating and maintenance expenses compared to the prior year
period, which was more than offset by increased operating and maintenance
expenses associated with the commencement of operations of our newbuild rigs and
maintenance and shipyard projects.&#160;&#160;As of March&#160;31, 2010, we had
reduced our total debt compared to December&#160;31, 2009, primarily due to
reduced borrowings under our commercial paper program (see &#8220;&#8212;Liquidity and
Capital Resources&#8212;Sources and Uses of Liquidity&#8221;).</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">For the year
ending December&#160;31, 2010, we expect our total revenues to decline slightly
compared to our total revenues for the year ended December&#160;31,
2009.&#160;&#160;We expect this reduction to result from reduced drilling
activity associated with stacked and idle rigs, lost revenues from the <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Deepwater&#160;Horizon</font>
contract termination and reduced operating activity associated with our
integrated services.&#160;&#160;However, we expect the decrease in revenues to
be partially offset by a full year of drilling operations of our
five&#160;newbuilds delivered in&#160;2009, the commencement of drilling
operations of four additional newbuilds in&#160;2010, and increased activity in
our other operations segment.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">Additionally,
we expect our total operating and maintenance expenses for the year ending
December&#160;31, 2010 to increase compared to operating and maintenance
expenses for the year ended December&#160;31, 2009 primarily due to a full year
of drilling operations of our five&#160;newbuilds delivered in 2009, the
commencement of drilling operations of four&#160;additional newbuilds
in&#160;2010, an increase in maintenance and shipyard projects, an increase in
activity in our other operations segment and additional costs associated with
the <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Deepwater&#160;Horizon</font>
incident.&#160;&#160;We expect these increases will be mostly offset by reduced
costs associated with stacked and idle rigs and reduced integrated services
activity.&#160;&#160;Our projected operating and maintenance expenses for the
year ending December&#160;31, 2010 remain uncertain and could be affected by
actual activity levels, rig reactivations, exchange rates and cost inflation as
well as other factors.</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">We are
currently evaluating the consequences of the <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Deepwater&#160;Horizon</font>
incident, which is expected to have a material effect on our results of
operations and cash flows and may have a material effect on our future
consolidated statement of financial position.&#160;&#160;Although our operating
and maintenance expenses for the year ending December&#160;31, 2010 will be
affected by the <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Deepwater&#160;Horizon</font>
incident, we cannot be certain of the extent of the resulting costs, related
insurance recoveries, or other consequences that the incident may have on our
operating results or cash flows.&#160;&#160;See &#8220;&#8212;Insurance matters&#8221; and
&#8220;Part&#160;II.&#160;&#160;Other Information, Item&#160;1A.&#160;&#160;Risk
Factors.&#8221;</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Insurance matters</font>&#8212;We
periodically evaluate our hull and machinery and third-party liability insurance
limits and self-insured retentions.&#160;&#160;Although our existing insurance
policies were scheduled to expire May&#160;1, 2010, we negotiated with our
underwriters a one-month extension as we assess the incident involving the loss
of our Ultra-Deepwater Floater <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Deepwater&#160;Horizon</font>.&#160;&#160;Although
we cannot provide any assurances, we are seeking to renew our hull and machinery
and third-party liability insurance coverages with provisions similar to
previous policies.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">Our
insurance program consisted of commercial market and captive insurance policies
primarily with 12 month policy periods beginning on May 1, 2009. Under the
program, we generally maintain a $125 million per occurrence deductible, limited
to a maximum of $250 million per year, on our hull and machinery. However, in
the event of a total loss or a constructive total loss of a drilling unit, such
loss would be subject to a deductible ranging from $0.5 million to $1.5 million.
Subject to the same shared deductible, we also have coverage for costs incurred
to mitigate damage to a rig&#160;up to&#160;an amount equal to 25 percent of a
rig&#8217;s insured value. Also subject to the same shared deductible, we have
coverage for wreck removal for up to 25 percent of a rig&#8217;s insured value, with
any excess generally covered to the extent of our excess liability coverage
described below.&#160;&#160;We carry $950 million of commercial market excess
liability coverage, exclusive of deductibles and self-insured
retention,&#160;noted below, which generally covers offshore risks such as
personal injury, third-party property claims, and third-party non-crew claims,
including wreck removal and pollution. We generally retain the risk for any
liability losses in excess of $1.0&#160;billion.&#160;&#160;Our excess liability
coverage has separate (1) $10 million per occurrence deductibles&#160;on crew
personal injury liability and on collision liability claims and (2) a separate
$5 million per occurrence deductible on&#160;other third-party non-crew claims.
These types of excess liability coverages are subject to an additional
aggregate&#160;self-insured retention&#160;of $50 million that is applied to any
occurrence in excess of the per occurrence deductible until the $50 million is
exhausted. We also carry $100 million of additional insurance that generally
covers expenses that would otherwise be assumed by the well owner, such as costs
to control the well, redrill expenses and pollution from the
well.&#160;&#160;This additional insurance provides coverage for such expenses
in circumstances in which we have legal or contractual liability arising from
our gross negligence and/or willful misconduct.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">We have
elected to self-insure operators extra expense coverage for ADTI and
CMI.&#160;&#160;This coverage provides protection against expenses related to
well control, pollution&#160;and redrill liability associated with
blowouts.&#160;&#160;Generally, ADTI&#8217;s customers assume, and indemnify ADTI for,
liability associated with blowouts in excess of $50 million.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">We generally
do not have commercial market insurance coverage for physical damage losses,
including liability for wreck removal expenses, to our fleet caused by named
windstorms in the U.S. Gulf of Mexico and war perils
worldwide.&#160;&#160;Except with respect to <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Dhirubhai Deepwater KG1</font> and
<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Dhirubhai Deepwater
KG2</font>, we generally do not carry insurance for loss of revenue unless
contractually required.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">In
April&#160;2010, following the sinking of the Ultra-Deepwater Floater <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Deepwater&#160;Horizon</font>, our
insurance underwriters declared the vessel a total loss.&#160;&#160;The rig had
an insured value of $560&#160;million, and we expect to receive these insurance
proceeds subject to a deductible ranging from $0.5&#160;million to
$1.5&#160;million.&#160;&#160;As of May&#160;5, 2010, we have received
$401&#160;million as partial payment&#160;of the expected insurance
recoveries.&#160;&#160;We carry insurance that covers wreck removal, if
required, subject to certain limits and deductibles.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

risk and &#8220;Part&#160;II.&#160;&#160;Other Information,
Item&#160;1A.&#160;&#160;Risk Factors.&#8221;</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Tax matters</font>&#8212;We are a Swiss
corporation and we operate through our various subsidiaries in a number of
countries throughout the world.&#160;&#160;Our tax provision is based upon and
subject to changes in the tax laws, regulations and treaties in effect in and
between the countries in which our operations are conducted and income is
earned.&#160;&#160;Our effective tax rate for financial reporting purposes
fluctuates from year to year, as our operations are conducted in different
taxing jurisdictions.&#160;&#160;A change in the tax laws, treaties or
regulations in any of the countries in which we operate, or in which we are
incorporated or resident, could result in a higher or lower effective tax rate
on our worldwide earnings and, as a result, could have a material effect on our
financial results.</font></div>

to our 2004 and 2005 U.S. federal income tax returns, the U.S. tax authorities
have withdrawn all of their previously proposed tax adjustments, except a claim
regarding transfer pricing for certain charters of drilling rigs between our
subsidiaries, reducing the total proposed adjustment to approximately
$79&#160;million, exclusive of interest.&#160;&#160;We believe an unfavorable
outcome on this assessment with respect to 2004 and 2005 activities would not
result in a material adverse effect on our consolidated financial position,
results of operations or cash flows.&#160;&#160;If the authorities were to
continue to pursue this position with respect to subsequent years and were
successful in such assertion, our effective tax rate on worldwide earnings with
respect to years following 2005 could increase substantially, and our earnings
and cash flows from operations could be materially and adversely
affected.&#160;&#160;Although we believe the transfer pricing for these charters
is materially correct, we have been unable to reach a resolution with the tax
authorities and we expect the matter to proceed to litigation.</font></div>

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Regulatory matters</font>&#8212;In
June&#160;2007, GlobalSantaFe Corporation&#8217;s (&#8220;GlobalSantaFe&#8221;) management
retained outside counsel to conduct an internal investigation of its Nigerian
and West African operations, focusing on brokers who handled customs matters
with respect to its affiliates operating in those jurisdictions and whether
those brokers have fully complied with the U.S. Foreign Corrupt Practices Act
(&#8220;FCPA&#8221;) and local laws.&#160;&#160;GlobalSantaFe commenced its investigation
following announcements by other oilfield service companies that they were
independently investigating the FCPA implications of certain actions taken by
third parties in respect of customs matters in connection with their operations
in Nigeria, as well as another company&#8217;s announced settlement implicating a
third party handling customs matters in Nigeria.&#160;&#160;In each case, the
customs broker was reported to be Panalpina<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">&#160;</font>Inc., which
GlobalSantaFe used to obtain temporary import permits for its rigs operating
offshore Nigeria.&#160;&#160;GlobalSantaFe voluntarily disclosed its internal
investigation to the U.S. Department of Justice (the &#8220;DOJ&#8221;) and the SEC and, at
their request, expanded its investigation to include the activities of its
customs brokers in certain other African countries.&#160; The investigation is
focusing on whether the brokers have fully complied with the requirements of
their contracts, local laws and the FCPA and GlobalSantaFe&#8217;s possible
involvement in any inappropriate or illegal conduct in connection with such
brokers.&#160;&#160;In late November<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">&#160;</font>2007,
GlobalSantaFe received a subpoena from the SEC for documents related to its
investigation.&#160; In addition, the SEC advised GlobalSantaFe that it had
issued a formal order of investigation.&#160; After the completion of the merger
with GlobalSantaFe, outside counsel began formally reporting directly to the
audit committee of our board of directors.&#160; Our legal representatives are
keeping the DOJ and SEC apprised of the scope and details of their investigation
and producing relevant information in response to their requests.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">On
July&#160;25, 2007, our legal representatives met with the DOJ in response to a
notice we received requesting such a meeting regarding our engagement of
Panalpina<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">&#160;</font>Inc. for freight
forwarding and other services in the U.S. and abroad.&#160;&#160;The DOJ
informed us that it was conducting an investigation of alleged FCPA violations
by oil service companies who used Panalpina<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">&#160;</font>Inc. and other
brokers in Nigeria and other parts of the world.&#160; We developed an
investigative plan which has continued to be amended and which would allow us to
review and produce relevant and responsive information requested by the DOJ and
SEC.&#160;&#160;The investigation was expanded to include one of our agents for
Nigeria.&#160;&#160;This investigation and the legacy GlobalSantaFe
investigation are being conducted by outside counsel who reports directly to the
audit committee of our board of directors.&#160;&#160;The investigation has
focused on whether the agent and the customs brokers have fully complied with
the terms of their respective agreements, the FCPA and local laws and the
company&#8217;s and its employees&#8217; possible involvement in any inappropriate or
illegal conduct in connection with such brokers and agent.&#160;&#160;Our
outside counsel has coordinated their efforts with the DOJ and the SEC with
respect to the implementation of our investigative plan, including keeping the
DOJ and SEC apprised of the scope and details of the investigation and producing
relevant information in response to their requests.&#160;&#160;The SEC has also
now issued a formal order of investigation in this case and issued a subpoena
for further information, including information related to the U.S. Treasury
Department&#8217;s Office of Foreign Assets Control (&#8220;OFAC&#8221;) investigation described
below.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">Our internal
compliance program has detected a potential violation of U.S. sanctions
regulations in connection with the shipment of goods to our operations in
Turkmenistan.&#160;&#160;Goods bound for our rig in Turkmenistan were shipped
through Iran by a freight forwarder.&#160;&#160;Iran is subject to a number of
economic regulations, including sanctions administered by OFAC, and
comprehensive restrictions on the export and re-export of U.S.-origin items to
Iran.&#160;&#160;Iran has been designated as a state sponsor of terrorism by the
U.S. State Department.&#160;&#160;Failure to comply with applicable laws and
regulations relating to sanctions and export restrictions may subject us to
criminal sanctions and civil remedies, including fines, denial of export
privileges, injunctions or seizures of our assets.&#160;&#160;We have
self-reported the potential violation to OFAC and retained outside counsel who
conducted an investigation of the matter and submitted a report to
OFAC.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">We are
continuing to cooperate with the DOJ, SEC and OFAC.&#160; We expect these
investigations will continue to result in the incurrence of significant legal
fees and related expenses as well as involve significant management
time.&#160;&#160;We cannot predict the ultimate outcome of these investigations,
the total costs to be incurred in completing the investigations, the potential
impact on personnel, the effect of implementing any further measures that may be
necessary to ensure full compliance with applicable laws or to what extent, if
at all, we could be subject to fines, sanctions or other
penalties.&#160;&#160;In response to these investigations, we have implemented
measures to strengthen and expand our compliance program and
training.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">
        <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
        <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">As a result
of the incident involving <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Deepwater&#160;Horizon</font>, the
Department of Homeland Security and the Department of Interior have announced a
joint investigation into the causes of the incident and its
effects.&#160;&#160;The U.S. Coast Guard and the Minerals Management Service
share jurisdiction over the investigation into the incident.&#160;&#160;We
cannot predict the ultimate outcome of these investigations, the total costs to
be incurred in completing the investigations, the potential impact on personnel,
the effect of implementing measures that may result from these investigations or
to what extent, if any, we could be subject to fines, sanctions or other
penalties.&#160;&#160;In addition, various committees and subcommittees of the
House of Representatives and the Senate of the United States have requested our
participation in hearings related to the incident.&#160;&#160;We have also
received a request to preserve information from the DOJ.&#160;&#160;We may also
face additional requests for participation in hearings from the Congress of the
United States with investigations from other governmental bodies.</font></div>
        <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
        <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
        <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Environmental matters</font>&#8212;On
April&#160;28, 2010, in connection with the <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Deepwater&#160;Horizon</font>
incident, one of our subsidiaries was notified by the U.S. Coast Guard that,
under the provisions of the Oil Pollution Act of 1990 (&#8220;OPA&#8221;), <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Deepwater&#160;Horizon</font> had
been designated as a source of&#160;oil discharges and our subsidiary has been
designated as a responsible party under OPA.&#160;&#160;In the notice, the U.S.
Coast Guard noted that its information indicates that oil discharges resulting
from the incident include discharges from <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Deepwater&#160;Horizon</font> on or
above the surface of the water and ongoing discharges from the well
head.&#160;&#160;Because the ongoing discharges from the well head are occurring
nearly a mile below the surface of the water, for which we believe we have no
responsibility under OPA, we have responded to the U.S. Coast Guard&#8217;s notice and
denied our subsidiary&#8217;s designation as a responsible party to the extent of any
underwater discharges from the well head.&#160;&#160;There can be no assurance
as to the ultimate outcome of this matter.</font></div>
        <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
        <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
        <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">See
&#8220;Part&#160;II.&#160;&#160;Other Information, Item&#160;1A.&#160;&#160;Risk
Factors.&#8221;</font></div>
        <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
        <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font id="TAB2" style="LETTER-SPACING: 9pt">&#160;&#160;&#160;</font>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;
</div>
        <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><font id="TAB2" style="LETTER-SPACING: 9pt">&#160;&#160;&#160;</font>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;
Other matters</font>&#8212;In addition, from time to time, we receive inquiries from
governmental regulatory agencies regarding our operations around the world,
including inquiries with respect to various tax, environmental, regulatory and
compliance matters.&#160;&#160;To the extent appropriate under the
circumstances, we investigate such matters, respond to such inquiries and
cooperate with the regulatory agencies.&#160;&#160;Although we are unable to
predict the outcome of any of these matters, we do not expect the liability, if
any, resulting from these inquiries to have a material adverse effect on our
consolidated statement of financial position, results of operations or cash
flows.</font></div>
      </div>

in the future, make significant capital commitments for such
purposes.&#160;&#160;We may also consider investments related to major rig
upgrades or new rig construction.&#160;&#160;Any such acquisition, upgrade or
new rig construction could involve the payment by us of a substantial amount of
cash or the issuance of a substantial number of additional shares or other
securities.&#160;&#160;During the three months ended March&#160;31, 2010, we
acquired <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">GSF&#160;Explorer</font>, an asset

$15&#160;million, thereby terminating the capital lease obligation.</font></div>

time, we may review possible dispositions of drilling units.&#160;&#160;During
the three months ended March&#160;31, 2010, we completed the sale of two
Midwater Floaters, <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">GSF&#160;Arctic&#160;II</font> and
<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">GSF&#160;Arctic&#160;IV</font>.&#160;&#160;In
connection with the sale, we received net cash proceeds of $38&#160;million and
non-cash proceeds in the form of two notes receivable in the aggregate amount of
$165&#160;million.&#160;&#160;The notes receivable, which are secured by the
drilling units, have stated interest rates of 9&#160;percent and are payable in
scheduled quarterly installments of principal and interest through maturity in
January&#160;2015.&#160;&#160;We estimated the fair values of the notes
receivable based on unobservable inputs that require significant judgment, for
which there is little or no market data.&#160;&#160;We continue to operate <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">GSF&#160;Arctic&#160;IV</font> under
a short-term bareboat charter with the new owner of the vessel through
October&#160;2010.&#160;&#160;As a result of the sale, we recognized a loss on
disposal of assets for the three months ended March&#160;31, 2010, in the amount

existing cash balances, internally generated cash flows, bank credit agreements
and proceeds from asset sales to fulfill anticipated obligations such as
scheduled debt maturities or other payments, repayment of debt due within one
year (including the repurchase of 1.625% Series A Notes at the option of the
noteholders), capital expenditures, shareholder-approved distributions and
working capital needs.&#160;&#160;Subject in each case to then existing market
conditions and to our then expected liquidity needs, among other factors, we may
continue to use a portion of our internally generated cash flows and proceeds
from asset sales to repurchase shares or reduce debt prior to scheduled
maturities through debt repurchases, either in the open market or in privately
negotiated transactions, through debt redemptions or tender offers, or through
repayments of bank borrowings.&#160;&#160;From time to time, we may also use
borrowings under bank lines of credit and under our commercial paper program to
maintain liquidity for short-term cash needs.</font></div>

&#8220;&#8212;Share repurchase program.&#8221;</font></div>

February&#160;16,&#160;2010, we announced that our board of directors has

in Swiss francs for an amount equivalent to approximately U.S.

January&#160;2011 and April&#160;2011.&#160;&#160;Distributions to shareholders
in the form of a reduction in par value of our shares are not subject to the
35<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">&#160;</font>percent
Swiss withholding tax.&#160;&#160;Shareholders will be paid in U.S. dollars
converted using an exchange rate determined by us approximately two business

in Swiss francs.&#160;&#160;If approved, we intend to fund such distributions

to debt and equity markets may be reduced or closed to us due to a variety of
events, including among others, credit rating agency downgrades of our debt,
industry conditions, general economic conditions, market conditions and market
perceptions of us and our industry.&#160;&#160;The economic downturn and related
financial market instability has had, and may continue to have, an impact on our
business and our financial condition.&#160;&#160;Our ability to access such
markets may be severely restricted at a time when we would like, or need, to
access such markets, which could have an impact on our flexibility to react to
changing economic and business conditions.&#160;&#160;The economic downturn
could have an impact on the lenders participating in our credit facilities or on
our customers, causing them to fail to meet their obligations to

a $2.0<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">&#160;</font>billion
five-year revolving credit facility under the Five-Year Revolving Credit
Facility Agreement dated November&#160;27, 2007 (the &#8220;Five-Year Revolving Credit
Facility&#8221;).&#160;&#160;The Five-Year Revolving Credit Facility includes
limitations on creating liens, incurring subsidiary debt, transactions with
affiliates, sale/leaseback transactions, mergers and the sale of substantially
all assets.&#160;&#160;The Five-Year Revolving Credit Facility also includes a
covenant imposing a maximum debt to tangible capitalization ratio of 0.6 to
1.0.&#160;&#160;As of March&#160;31, 2010, our debt to tangible capitalization
ratio was 0.47 to 1.0.&#160;&#160;Borrowings under the Five-Year Revolving
Credit Facility are subject to acceleration upon the occurrence of events of
default.&#160;&#160;We are also subject to various covenants under the
indentures pursuant to which our public debt was issued, including restrictions
on creating liens, engaging in sale/leaseback transactions and engaging in
certain merger, consolidation or reorganization transactions.&#160;&#160;A
default under our public debt indentures could trigger a default under the
Five-Year Revolving Credit Facility and, if not waived by the lenders, could
cause us to lose access to the Five-Year Revolving Credit Facility and the
commercial paper program for which it provides liquidity.&#160;&#160;As of
April&#160;26, 2010, we had $81&#160;million in letters of credit issued and
outstanding and no borrowings outstanding under the Five-Year Revolving Credit
Facility.</font></div>

between our contract backlog and our debt, general market conditions and other
factors, that we should retain cash, reduce debt, make capital investments or
otherwise use cash for general corporate purposes, and consequently, repurchase
fewer or no shares under this program.&#160;&#160;Decisions regarding the
amount, if any, and timing of any share repurchases would be made from time to
time based upon these factors.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
        <div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
          <div id="FTR">
            <div style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left">
              <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">-&#160;32&#160;-</font></div>

          <div id="HDR">
            <div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; COLOR: #000000; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow"><a href="#Index">Index</a></font></div>
          </div>
        </div><br></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">Any shares
repurchased under this program are expected to be purchased from time to time
either, with respect to the U.S. market, from market participants that have
acquired those shares on the open market and that can fully recover Swiss
withholding tax resulting from the share repurchase or, with respect to the
Swiss market, on the second trading line for our shares on the SIX Swiss
Exchange.&#160;&#160;Repurchases could also be made by tender offer, in
privately negotiated transactions or by any other share repurchase
method.&#160;&#160;Any repurchased shares would be held by us for cancellation
by the shareholders at a future annual general meeting.&#160;&#160;The share
repurchase program could be suspended or discontinued by our board of directors
or company management, as applicable, at any time.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">Under Swiss
corporate law, the right of a company and its subsidiaries to repurchase and
hold its own shares is limited.&#160;&#160;A company may repurchase such
company&#8217;s shares to the extent it has freely distributable reserves as shown on
its Swiss statutory balance sheet in the amount of the purchase price and the
aggregate par value of all shares held by the company as treasury shares does
not exceed 10&#160;percent of the company&#8217;s share capital recorded in the Swiss
commercial register, whereby for purposes of determining whether the
10&#160;percent threshold has been reached, shares repurchased under a share
repurchase program for cancellation purposes authorized by the company&#8217;s
shareholders are disregarded.&#160;&#160;As of April&#160;26, 2010,
Transocean&#160;Inc., our wholly owned subsidiary, held as treasury shares
approximately four&#160;percent of our issued shares.&#160;&#160;At the annual
general meeting in May&#160;2009, the shareholders approved the release of
3.5&#160;billion Swiss francs of additional paid-in capital to other reserves,
or freely available reserves as presented on our Swiss statutory balance sheet,
to create the freely available reserve necessary for the 3.5&#160;billion Swiss
franc share repurchase program for the purpose of the cancellation of shares
(the &#8220;Currently Approved Program&#8221;).&#160;&#160;We may only repurchase shares to
the extent freely distributable reserves are available.&#160;&#160;Our board of
directors could, to the extent freely distributable reserves are available,
authorize the repurchase of additional shares for purposes other than
cancellation, such as to retain treasury shares for use in satisfying our
obligations in connection with incentive plans or other rights to acquire our
shares.&#160;&#160;Based on the current amount of shares held as treasury
shares, approximately six&#160;percent of our issued shares could be repurchased
for purposes of retention as additional treasury shares.&#160;&#160;Although our
board of directors has not approved such a share repurchase program for the
purpose of retaining repurchased shares as treasury shares, if it did so, any
such shares repurchased would be in addition to any shares repurchased under the
Currently Approved Program.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Distribution
recommendation</font>&#8212;Our board of directors has recommended that shareholders
at our May&#160;2010 annual general meeting approve a distribution in the form
of a par value reduction denominated in Swiss francs equal to approximately
$3.11&#160;per share.&#160;&#160;The distribution will, if approved, be paid in
four installments with expected payment dates in July&#160;2010,
October&#160;2010, January&#160;2011 and
April&#160;2011.&#160;&#160;Distributions to shareholders in the form of a
reduction in par value of our shares are not subject to the 35<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">&#160;</font>percent Swiss
withholding tax.&#160;&#160;Shareholders will be paid in U.S. dollars converted
using an exchange rate determined by us approximately two business days prior to
the payment date, unless shareholders elect to receive the payment in Swiss
francs.&#160;&#160;If approved, we intend to fund such distributions using our
cash flows from operations.</font></div>

there have been no material changes from the contractual obligations as

      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Operating revenues</font>&#8212;Contract
drilling revenues decreased primarily due to lower utilization during the three
months ended March&#160;31, 2010, as compared to the three months ended
March&#160;31, 2009, partly offset by higher average daily revenue during the
three months ended March&#160;31, 2010, as compared to the three months ended
March&#160;31, 2009.&#160;&#160;The lower utilization was primarily due to
reduced activity from 33 rigs stacked or idle as of March&#160;31, 2010,
compared to six rigs stacked or idle, including one held for sale, as of
March&#160;31, 2009, and higher out-of-service time for shipyard, mobilization,
maintenance and repair projects in the three months ended March&#160;31, 2010,
as compared to the same period in 2009.&#160;&#160;This reduced activity was
partially offset by the commencement of operations of our newbuilds in the three
months ended March&#160;31, 2010.&#160;&#160;Our average daily revenue increases
as we stack rigs in our Midwater Floaters and Jackups fleets, since rigs in
these classes are typically contracted at lower dayrates compared to those in
our High-Specification Floaters fleet.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">Contract
drilling intangible revenues declined $71&#160;million for the three months
ended March&#160;31, 2010, compared to the three months ended March&#160;31,
2009, due to timing of the contracts with which they were
associated.&#160;&#160;Contract drilling intangible revenues represent the
amortization of the fair value of drilling contracts in effect at the time of
our merger with GlobalSantaFe.&#160;&#160;We recognize contract drilling
intangible revenues over the respective contract period using the straight-line
method of amortization.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow">Other
revenues for the three months ended March&#160;31, 2010 decreased primarily due
to reduced activity in our other operations segment.</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Arial Narrow"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Costs and expenses</font>&#8212;Operating
and maintenance expenses increased primarily due to increases in shipyard and
maintenance projects and the commencement of operations of our
newbuilds.&#160;&#160;These increases were partially offset by a greater number
of stacked rigs in the three months ended March&#160;31, 2010, reduced activity
in our other operations segment and reduced overhead expenses.</font></div>
